title: Ukraine: Building Climate Resilience in Agriculture and Forestry
temporal_coverage: Observations mainly from the 1980s onward and RCP projections through 2100.
methodology: Climate-model ensemble across approximately 7,400 grid points with sector and distributional modelling.
limitations: Prepared before the full-scale invasion, uses older RCPs, and has no war-adjusted exposure baseline.

title: Ukraine's Climate Change Adaptation Communication to UNFCCC
organization: Government of Ukraine and United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change
geographic_coverage: Ukraine, national and sectoral with some subnational references
temporal_coverage: Historical evidence and policy status mainly through 2023-2024, with projections to 2100.
methodology: Official synthesis of climate risks, policy arrangements, barriers, needs, and sector priorities.
limitations: Mostly repackages pre-invasion assessments and has limited post-2022 quantitative risk updating.

title: Ukraine Fifth Rapid Damage and Needs Assessment: February 2022-December 2025
organization: Government of Ukraine, World Bank Group, European Commission and United Nations
geographic_coverage: Ukraine, with sector, oblast and hromada detail where available
temporal_coverage: Damage through 31 December 2025, losses with an 18-month projection, and needs for 2026-2035.
methodology: Joint administrative, engineering, remote-sensing, partner, and modelling assessment using sector damage, loss, and needs methods.
limitations: Occupied and frontline data are incomplete, methods evolve, and needs are not outcomes or firm finance commitments.

title: Status of Environment and Climate in Ukraine: Assessing the Impact of War and Implications for Reconstruction
geographic_coverage: Ukraine, with mapped subnational and ecosystem evidence
methodology: Multi-source environmental synthesis using remote sensing, administrative data, mapped analysis, and policy review.
limitations: Coverage is weakest in occupied and combat areas and attribution among climate, warfare, and land management is often limited.

title: Attacks against Ukraine's Energy Infrastructure and Update on the Human Rights Situation in Ukraine, 1 December 2025-31 May 2026
organization: Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights
geographic_coverage: Government-controlled Ukraine and selected affected cities and facilities
methodology: Field monitoring, 180 visits, 1,926 interviews overall, and specialized energy-impact visits and interviews.
limitations: No direct occupied-territory access; seasonal cold and heat are not attributed to climate change.

title: Rapid Environmental Assessment of Kakhovka Dam Breach, Ukraine, 2023
organization: United Nations Environment Programme and UNEP-DHI
geographic_coverage: Lower Dnipro, Kakhovka reservoir, downstream and irrigation-dependent areas
methodology: Remote sensing, hydrological analysis, partner data, desk evidence, and expert assessment under access constraints.
limitations: Many impacts were modelled or preliminary; the breach is a conflict-related infrastructure disaster, not a climate event.

title: Impact of the Russia-Ukraine Armed Conflict on Water Resources and Water Infrastructure
geographic_coverage: Ukraine, concentrated in eastern and southern incident evidence
temporal_coverage: Mainly the first three months after 24 February 2022.
methodology: Systematic compilation of realized and potential impacts from verified public reports and supplementary evidence.
limitations: Early-war and undercounted snapshot with reporting bias and no climate attribution.

title: Rebuilding Ukraine by Reinforcing Regional and Municipal Governance
organization: Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development
temporal_coverage: Primarily pre-February 2022 capacity evidence interpreted for recovery.
methodology: Surveys of 741 municipalities, 119 rayons and 24 oblasts plus Kyiv, with administrative and efficiency analysis.
limitations: Pre-full-scale-war, partly self-reported baseline; current municipal capacity can differ substantially.

title: Final Evaluation of Mykolaiv Recovered
organization: United Nations Development Programme Evaluation Resource Centre / external evaluation team
geographic_coverage: Mykolaiv Oblast and participating municipalities and institutions
temporal_coverage: Project from July 2023 through December 2025; evaluation October 2025-February 2026.
methodology: External mixed-method final evaluation using interviews, document review, site evidence, and participant surveys.
limitations: Limited counterfactual and causal attribution, low response rates for some surveys, and no national generalizability.

title: Ukraine: Reframing the Narrative of Climate, Environmental Degradation and Conflict
organization: adelphi / Weathering Risk / International Rescue Committee
geographic_coverage: Ukraine, with southern, eastern and community examples
methodology: Desk review, expert consultations, and qualitative pathway synthesis.
limitations: Expert synthesis rather than causal evaluation; some chains rely on secondary evidence and remain inferential.

title: Priorities for Agricultural Support in Ukraine
geographic_coverage: Ukraine, national and agroecological with east-central hotspots
temporal_coverage: War context through 2024 with climate scenarios at 1.5 and 3 degrees Celsius warming.
methodology: Agricultural-sector review, policy analysis, and model-derived green-water-scarcity estimates.
limitations: Some modelling was forthcoming, scenario results are not observed impacts, and exposure is not fully war-adjusted.

title: Policy Brief: State Strategy on Internal Displacement
organization: United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees Ukraine
geographic_coverage: Ukraine, national, regional and community implementation
methodology: Review of the adopted strategy, legal framework, targets, responsibilities, and implementation arrangements.
limitations: Newly adopted policy; first formal assessment is due in 2027 and financing and local delivery remain uncertain.
